# How To Use Loops

Source: [4841](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/4841); edited 2024-11-26. Evidence: archived documentation.

Not independently verified in the current game. An article edit date is not a behavioral test date.

<a id="wiki-4841-n1"></a>

- Rule loops repeat an entire action list; While/End repeat a scoped block and then continue with subsequent actions.

<a id="wiki-4841-n2"></a>

- Repeated/unbounded loops need waits to pace work and avoid exhausting server execution; bounded small for-loops can intentionally run without waits.

<a id="wiki-4841-n3"></a>

- For-loop example iterates zero-based array indices from zero to Count Of exclusive and applies per-target operations separately.

<a id="wiki-4841-n4"></a>

- Use a player-owned loop index/state for concurrently running Each Player loops.

Source limitations:

- Article describes a 0.016-second minimum wait and unconditional no-wait crash behavior; preserve as archived guidance, not a precise modern scheduling proof.

- For-loop prose assumes positive steps and describes condition check after body; empty/reversed ranges and negative steps require authoritative action-level verification.
